approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules. It keeps a bounded score-greedy breeding population, draws parents from high-ranked score bands, and uses connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations with ordinary continuation. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical admission and duplicate rejection form a surplus pool. A Gaussian process using counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity fits every accepted observation; the same current archive supplies the score mean and scale. Correlated function draws select the evaluated batch. Each real accepted offspring immediately updates the full archive, survivors and subsequent breeding.
approach.novelty: Remove generated records only from the GP conditioning matrix while continuing to compute normalization from every current accepted raw score. The training cohort becomes immutable copies of the usable initial records, but its standardized targets, raw predictions and uncertainty can still respond to the current normalizer. One earlier sibling froze membership and normalization together; another froze normalization with full membership. This is their missing consumer split. It tests whether generated conditioning rows contribute when adaptive normalization and live genetic feedback remain present, without repeating either earlier control.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-62daf219c70a routes newly accepted scores simultaneously into GP conditioning and score normalization, so its successful predictive allocation does not identify the contribution of generated conditioning rows alone. The actual three summary.json and run.log files are complete and successful: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Read-only task-log auditing finds 435 fits whose chronological training membership grows from the usable initial cohort through the pre-final archive, 4200 generated accepted records with a later fit, and 150 final records without a later fit opportunity; there are 629 parent-beating offspring and 258 sequential incumbent advances. These local counts are not endpoint contribution evidence. The complete initial-membership/initial-normalization control n-7de8feaf821f loses 0.15185627363148665 with all fifteen endpoints lower; it bundles membership, generated-label conditioning and normalization. The complete full-membership/initial-normalization control n-c963c9fc454a loses 0.034355391271028345, with ten endpoint losses, five gains and seed signs loss/gain/loss. Its current interpretation supports the joint ongoing mean-and-scale module conditional on full conditioning. Neither result answers the missing initial-membership/current-normalization contrast, and subtracting their losses cannot answer it. The full-pool generation-order control n-01b48dd09404 loses 0.12438789088524467 but concerns composite predictive allocation, not this membership consumer. The limitation being addressed is an unresolved dependency inside the Parent's retained learning loop, not an established failure of its GP to execute.
hypothesis: Remove generated accepted records only from active GP conditioning by fitting immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted cohort, while recomputing the inherited score mean and scale from the full current accepted archive at every original fit call and retaining immediate live genetic feedback.

finding_summary.headline: Generated conditioning rows contribute: removing them lowers the mean by 0.22566
finding_summary.insights:
Generated conditioning records have positive conditional value even when adaptive normalization, score-based survival and recursive breeding remain available. This answers the missing membership question without treating the intervention as removal of all online learning. The same-input reference had lower prediction error on the actual scored molecules, but it supplies no rewards for omitted alternatives and no alternative future history; prediction error, reuse and uncertainty changes do not identify the route to the endpoint loss.

The earlier joint freeze and normalization-only findings remain intact. With complete matched outcomes and source boundaries checked, the four-treatment arithmetic interaction is +0.108156. Initial-only conditioning with current normalization scored 0.073800 below the jointly frozen version, while the historical full-conditioning comparison supported current normalization. The sign therefore depends on the conditioning context in these observations. This descriptive comparison shares one control, retains mixed task-level interaction signs, and establishes neither independent replication nor additive or mediated effects.

The molecular assessment finds persistent sulfur-rich, heavily halogenated docking families where the Parent reached more conventional aryl/amine arrangements, and more tiny fragments on every task. Useful aromatic amides and alternative ring arrangements still occur. These chemical associations help describe the weaker search outcomes but do not attribute them to one motif or prove a chemical mediator. Bond plausibility, ring geometry, stereochemical identity and the broader graph-evolution contribution remain open.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 fits kept the same ten initial records in exact order while normalization used the growing accepted archive. The 4,200 generated records with a later fit never entered conditioning, but all entered normalization; 150 final records had no later opportunity. Every first batch matched the Parent exactly. After feedback, all 420 later sets differed from a full-conditioning reference on the same saved pools and normal draws. Of 3,608 actual accepted choices absent from those reference sets, 3,475 later entered normalization and 1,146 later bred. Across all offspring, 1,626 identities served as later parents, so feedback remained active outside conditioning.

All fifteen task runs completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.370013, a paired change of -0.225656 against the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.245204, -0.221990 and -0.209774. Fourteen endpoints and all five task means declined; zaleplon in seed 2 increased by 0.001361. Docking had the largest mean decrease, from 0.998989 to 0.298274. The Child still made 511 strict generating-parent wins and 118 incumbent advances, versus 629 and 258 for the Parent. These local successes did not preserve its endpoint.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families coexist with fragment loss, unusual heteroatom bonds and crowded, stereochemically unresolved rings
molecular.overall_character: Node n-c2f46c40bbba produces substituted indole amides and open diaryl enamides, linked aza-aromatic carbonyl systems, halogenated sulfur-rich aryl structures, dense nitrogen/carbonyl polycycles, and smaller unsaturated polar fragments. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent n-62daf219c70a Search trajectory files were read in full, covering every task and seeds 0, 1 and 2. No paths or task comparisons are missing. The immutable brief explicitly reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with all issued seeds matched and no profile mismatch. Initial molecule/score records match within each task/seed. Each Child task contains 900 observations, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every optimizer SMILES parsed in the offline RDKit audit, which is graph validity rather than evidence of synthesis, stability or binding. Digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.7011 to 0.9621 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.5103 to 0.9391; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Neutral strings nevertheless contain amines, and many saturated or bridged centres have unresolved stereochemical identity. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds, while leaders repeatedly occupy a narrower family within a seed. Unique SMILES do not establish independent plausible scaffolds. The clearest paired chemical difference is persistent sulfur-rich, often highly halogenated Child chemistry versus more conventional aryl/aliphatic-amine Parent leaders on one task; other tasks show different departures rather than a single universal missing group. Tiny-fragment proposals are also more common: in fixed task order, Child counts with at most four heavy atoms are 65, 89, 65, 27 and 93, versus Parent counts 25, 25, 32, 13 and 24, each out of 870 proposals. Sizes and bond counts here are derived solely from the supplied SMILES using RDKit 2023.09.6; scores are copied from trajectories and never recomputed. The supporting molecular-evidence-audit.json is in .slots/round-0025-slot-3/. The digest final_molecules excerpt is late seed-2 output, not the retained best molecule of every seed; full trajectories supply seed-specific leaders and late counterexamples. Parent chemistry comparisons below cite published seed/evaluation records by description; every cited_smiles entry comes from the Child digest or the immutable trusted Child citation paths. Transferable gaps preserve their recorded origin in n-c55c3d520a2c, their reproduction in n-62daf219c70a, and the current Search conditions. Their recurrence is a chemical association, not component attribution, activation evidence or a contribution decision.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 leads with a conventional methoxy/dimethyl indole carboxanilide bearing carbon-bound fluorine: 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Seed 1 retains the indole/anilide organization but adds bromine and an N-F bond; its leader has 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Seed 2 instead leads with a 26-heavy-atom, two-benzene framework: a methoxy/methyl benzonitrile linked through an amino-substituted alkene and amide to a chlorofluorobenzyl region. The whole proposal set has median 25 heavy atoms and range 1 to 50; digest mean SMILES length is 38.7, ring-string incidence 0.9195 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9023. The ordinary seed-0 amide and carbon-bound halogens in the seed-2 leader are real plausibility counterexamples to the N-halogen liability. The latter still contains a tautomer-sensitive aminoalkene with unspecified alkene geometry. Published Parent seeds instead lead with a fused-ring amino-cumulene, an N-hydroxy pyridyl indole amide, and an indole/aryl diketone, respectively; the Child has retained familiar aromatic chemistry while changing its functional arrangement.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader has an N-F bond on the heteroaromatic nitrogen. Nearby output includes N-N substitution and peroxide-bearing ethers; these differ chemically from ordinary aryl C-F.
The seed-2 aminoalkene family has possible enamine/imine tautomerism and unspecified geometric identity. A reasonable carbon skeleton does not establish a stable isolated form.
Late proposals include methane, interhalogens and strongly truncated aromatic fragments after larger useful arrangements have already appeared.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the favorable aromatic/polar combination is missing in fragmented late proposals; neither rings nor amide chemistry are globally absent.

The Parent pyridyl/carbonyl arrangements and the Child open diaryl family show multiple possible organizations, but the record does not establish a common stable, chemically independent alternative that preserves their favorable scores across seeds.
Alkene geometry and tautomeric identity of the aminoalkene family are unresolved; the trajectories do not establish that specifying either would increase the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed leaders are 0.38277504802042894 at evaluation 225, 0.3974929831413733 at evaluation 97, and 0.4403336603489188 at evaluation 136. Their matched Parent leaders are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081, respectively: seed 2 is a counterexample to a uniform decrease. Seed-2 evaluations 27 and 257 substitute carbon-bound F versus Br on the same diaryl aminoacrylamide and share exactly 0.391794428949253. The score does not uniquely reward fluorine in that pair. The retained second aromatic/carbonyl region matters in the observed comparisons: the smaller aminoalkene/dinitrile at evaluation 297 scores 0.0006818853688024546, while methane and FBr reach 0.0. Adding an amino substituent to the seed-2 best framework gives 0.3226220164001652 at evaluation 299. Extra nitrogen is therefore not uniformly rewarded. These are local structural associations, not identification of the hidden objective or proof of any required reactive bond.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 leads with a 28-heavy-atom fused nitrogen dione linked to an aromatic-labelled ten-membered nitrogen-rich ring, carrying O-Br, O-F and N-F bonds. Seed 1 leads with a more recognizable 32-heavy-atom linked aza-aromatic system: a fused O/N carbonyl heterocycle, pyridyl/diazine regions, a nitrile, methoxy groups and vinyl/methyl substitution. Seed 2 favors two pyridyl regions joined by an NH group, with an ester and an O-N(F)-N=O substituent; its ethyl-ester leader has 26 heavy atoms. Whole-set heavy atoms range from 1 to 115 with median 29; the corresponding Parent median is 33. The digest reports mean SMILES length 54.3, maximum length 232, ring-string incidence 0.8736 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8701. A large seed-1 evaluation-233 oligomer of repeated aromatic carbonyl heterocycles has 86 heavy atoms and twelve perceived rings. The published Parent seed-0 high-score family instead links a compact nitrogen/carbonyl/thione core to a fused aza-aromatic group. Other Parent seeds use related linked aza-aromatics or peroxide-containing aryl assemblies. The Parent chemistry also retains clear local reactivity concerns.
liabilities: The seed-0 leader combines O-Br, O-F and N-F with a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; aromatic graph perception is insufficient evidence of its conformation or synthetic accessibility.
The seed-2 leader contains both N-F and N-nitroso connectivity in an O-N(F)-N=O unit. Its score does not validate stability or medicinal acceptability.
Late ketene-containing, N-N-bearing and tiny heteroatom proposals persist; repeated heteroaromatic oligomers create a separate size and synthesis concern.
missing_features: The compact, linked nitrogen-rich organization of the published Parent seed-0 leader is not recovered as a Child leading family. Its presence in the Parent does not identify a uniquely required core or substituent.

Consistent stable peripheral chemistry is missing among leaders, although the seed-1 leader and the near-leading seed-2 aryl-ether assembly show that useful scored structures can omit heteroatom-halogen bonds.
Reliable size control while retaining linked functional regions is not shown: very large repeated ring assemblies compete with compact examples without a corresponding score advantage.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child leaders at seed/evaluation 0/273, 1/280 and 2/226 score 0.5943125788327026, 0.6043543077209765 and 0.6026929759245471; published Parent leaders score 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The pronounced seed-0 difference accompanies a different linked-ring organization, not an absence of nitrogen or rings. The seed-2 propyl ester at evaluation 278 ties the ethyl ester exactly at 0.6026929759245471, and a carbon-fluorinated diarylamine/aryl-ether assembly at evaluation 289 reaches 0.6003972356750286 without the N-F/nitroso appendage. The 86-heavy-atom oligomer scores 0.6003060183611016, slightly below the much smaller seed-1 leader: elaboration is not a reliable positive gradient. FOCl and methyl bromide lie at 0.5; the small N/O chain at final seed-2 evaluation 299 scores 0.5008805917576611. These floor-like values do not establish useful molecular chemistry. The visible association favors combined heteroaromatic arrangements over isolated fragments, with little discrimination among some peripheral changes.

per_task.generated_character: The Child remains strongly halogenated and sulfur-rich. Seed 0 leads with a 29-heavy-atom polyunsaturated carbocyclic/diaryl structure carrying an aryl O-S(=N)-aryl linkage and chlorinated alkene substituents; it lacks an ordinary aliphatic amine. Its next leader has a primary aminoalkyl chain on a smaller related aryl/sulfur framework. Seed 1 instead leads with a 37-heavy-atom, densely connected nitrogen-ring structure bearing carboxylic acid, thiol and N-hydroxy sulfur-oxo functionality. Seed 2 leads with 32 heavy atoms: amino-substituted chlorophenyl groups and saturated nitrogen rings connected through sulfur-oxo groups, with both free and sulfonyl-bound nitrogens. Median heavy-atom count is 31, identical to the Parent, but the Child range extends to 113; digest mean SMILES length is 62.9 and halogen-string incidence 0.9701. Ring-string incidence 0.8759 and aromatic-string incidence 0.8379 exclude any ring-deficiency account. Published Parent leaders have substantially more conventional flexible tertiary-amine or substituted pyrrolidine/aryl arrangements. The Child therefore misses their consistent organization, rather than the raw ability to emit nitrogen or saturated rings. Both panels still include heavy halogenation and unspecified stereochemistry.
liabilities: Unusual aryl O-S(=N)-aryl and N-hydroxy sulfur-oxo environments coexist with heavily chlorinated unsaturation; a valid valence graph does not establish a routine stable compound.
Seed-1 leading connectivity includes a small fused nitrogen ring and dense unsaturation; other examples extend into repeated sulfur/nitrogen assemblies of doubtful synthetic practicality.
Some nitrogen centres are sulfonyl-bound while others are free. Treating all nitrogen atoms or all neutral structures as equivalent would erase a chemically relevant distinction.

The seed-0 leader is a counterexample to the claim that every Child leader requires a conventional aliphatic amine, and the seed-2 leader is a counterexample to the claim that such centres cannot be generated.
missing_features: The Child does not reliably reproduce the Parent combination of conventional available aliphatic amines with appropriately connected aromatic regions; free amines already occur in Child examples, so the gap is conditional organization rather than an absent atom class.
Conventional sulfur and nitrogen environments that preserve the better-scoring aryl arrangement are not consistently shown among the Child leaders.
The saturated rings, substituted methines and crowded bridges lack explicit stereochemical identity. Neutral notation does not establish that their amines are unprotonatable.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed/evaluation leaders 0/277, 1/221 and 2/222 score 0.39825526834111996, 0.24819253402023553 and 0.24837317476984055. Their published Parent counterparts reach 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012 with aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangements. Within Child output, the aminoalkyl relative at seed 0/evaluation 290 scores 0.38325316908312185, close to the amine-free leader. This prevents a simple claim that adding an amine is sufficient or that every useful molecule needs one. The very low tail contains sulfonyl-bound cyclic nitrogen with ester, acid or acyl groups: seed 1/evaluation 58 scores 0.00016747245492913543, and seed 0/evaluation 16 scores 0.00021169315013374197. Seed 0/evaluation 201, an N-alkoxy sulfonamide, reaches 0.00011936470435483337. Aromatic chlorine, sulfur-oxo groups and nitrogen count alone thus explain neither high nor low reward. A much larger linked nitrogen/sulfur structure at seed 2/evaluation 299 scores 0.031101959702800542, and the final seed-2 proposal scores 0.05974895974643189. The observed gradients favor particular arrangements and exposure of functional groups over indiscriminate growth; no binding, protonation or chemical-mediation claim follows.

per_task.generated_character: Output is dominated by nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems appended to aromatic regions. Seed 0 leads with a 32-heavy-atom dense fused/bridged and spiro-like framework containing N-N bonds and cyclic carbonyl nitrogens; RDKit perceives seven rings. Seed 1 leads with a 28-heavy-atom fused aromatic/polycyclic N-methyl dicarbonyl structure, an N-propyl group and a hydroxyl-bearing small-ring junction. Seed 2 leads with a 36-heavy-atom ester/ethoxy-substituted phenyl region attached through a nitrogen-containing bicyclic dione to a hydroxypyridyl group. Its higher saturated-carbon content does not remove questions about stereochemistry and access to the connected rings. The whole-set heavy-atom median is 31 and range 1 to 73. Ring-string incidence 0.9621, aromatic-string incidence 0.9391 and halogen incidence 0.1126 describe a highly cyclic, relatively lightly halogenated stream; mean SMILES length is 56.3. Parent leaders also combine aromatic regions with partly saturated nitrogen/carbonyl rings, particularly quinoline-linked arrangements in seeds 1 and 2, so the Child is not missing rings or carbonyl acceptors in general.
liabilities: Small-ring junctions, medium-ring closures, bridges and N-N-containing dicarbonyl rings require environment-specific feasibility assessment.
Late output includes an extended peroxide chain and N-fluorination of a carbonyl heterocycle, neither of which is validated by retained aromatic character.
A higher perceived ring count can accompany lower supplied reward; ring richness is not a proxy for either synthetic plausibility or productive scaffold coverage.
missing_features: The favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl functions are present, but reliable geometrically credible and synthetically simpler alternatives preserving their arrangement are not established at the better Parent scores.
Potential stereogenic saturated and bridged centres remain unspecified; aromatic labels and perceived ring counts do not determine a feasible conformation.
Independent plausible scaffold families with the same favorable functional arrangement are limited among leaders within each seed; cross-seed differences prevent a claim of total structural collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Child seed leaders at evaluations 278, 297 and 252 score 0.17962290706107803, 0.19821177233257764 and 0.20087346816433777. Published Parent seed leaders score 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. The Child seed-2 hydroxypyridyl leader has a close hydroxyphenyl counterpart at evaluation 297 scoring 0.19790700347467463. This small local difference supports the combined aromatic/dicarbonyl arrangement more strongly than an assertion that one ring nitrogen is a universal missing requirement. Methane and ethene reach 0.0; the short peroxide chain at seed 2/evaluation 295 scores 0.011451966686277362. The final seed-2 N-fluorinated fused dione scores 0.17151713254808326, below its incumbent despite keeping substantial ring and carbonyl content. The seven-ring seed-0 leader also remains below the less densely cyclic seed-2 leader. More rings, more reactive substitution or greater complexity do not create a uniform positive gradient.

per_task.generated_character: This is the least consistently aromatic Child stream: aromatic-string incidence is 0.5103, ring-string incidence 0.7011, and median heavy-atom count 20 versus Parent 27. Child sizes range from 1 to 62 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length is 36.6. Seed 0 leads with a 22-heavy-atom furan attached to an unsaturated amino chain containing an N-fluoro group and an N-ethyl/N-formyl amide region. Seed 1 leads with a 22-heavy-atom nonaromatic unsaturated oxygen ring bearing an ester, fluorinated/chlorinated substituents and a brominated amino-acetal-like carbon attached to an N-N chain. Seed 2 leads with a 24-heavy-atom dense bridged nitrogen polycycle containing imino, enolic, N-N, N-F and fluorovinyl functionality; it has six perceived rings but only one aromatic ring. A nearby high scorer instead has a methylthio substituent on ring nitrogen and a carbonyl-containing core. Parent leaders are fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles, including the seed-2 small cyclic-cumulene family. The Child changes the chemistry toward smaller fragments in some seeds and a dense cage in another; this is not a uniform recovery of a conventional drug-like scaffold.
liabilities: The seed-2 leading cage has several potentially stereogenic junctions, a small-ring connection and dense unsaturation. Parsing alone cannot demonstrate an accessible geometry or synthesis.
N-F, N-N, N-S and brominated amino-acetal-like environments occur among the leaders; recognizable ester, amide or furan groups do not resolve those separate liabilities.

Cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0126 in Child output, lower than the published Parent value 0.0517. The leading Child cage is noncumulated, a counterexample to simply transferring the Parent cyclic-cumulene description to this node.
All seed-2 final examples are proposals rather than replacements for the retained best; a late elaborate structure can score close to zero.
missing_features: Reliable assembly of a compact, balanced polar framework is missing across seeds: successful compact examples coexist with near-zero fragments and oversized repeated heterocycles.

Geometrically credible and conventionally bonded alternatives preserving the better-scoring composition are not established among the highest-scoring cage examples; the Parent also has geometry and reactivity liabilities.

Stereochemical, tautomeric and alkene-geometric identity are unresolved in the saturated bridges, enolic regions and imino/fluoroalkene motifs. Their absence is not a measured cause of the score difference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child seed/evaluation leaders 0/295, 1/297 and 2/227 score 0.3460713746323746, 0.24612446414743272 and 0.46251220941540966; published Parent leaders score 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. The seed-2 methylthio/carbonyl cage at evaluation 191 reaches 0.441278750217193 without an N-F bond, so that reactive bond is not a universal requirement even within this cage family. The oversized repeated heterocyclic ester from seed 1/evaluation 30 scores 7.736617345169896e-55, while the small chloromethyl sulfide at seed 2/evaluation 298 scores 9.045714876459341e-20. Neither indiscriminate growth nor collapse to a tiny halogenated fragment is rewarded. A related nitrogen cage at the final seed-2 evaluation scores only 6.3240862403421795e-06 despite retaining dense rings and fluorinated unsaturation. The gradient is consistent with a constrained combination of size, polar-group placement and substitution; it does not establish an exact missing pharmacophore, a fluorine-count rule, or validation of the leading cage geometry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c, was reproduced in published n-62daf219c70a, and recurs in n-c2f46c40bbba under Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 with 300 observations per task. Current leaders include N-F, O-F, O-Br, N-nitroso, N-N and unusual sulfur environments. Counterexamples include the conventional N-H indole amide and the linked aza-aromatic nitrile leader without heteroatom-halogen bonds. These are environment-specific concerns, not evidence that rings, amines or ordinary carbon-bound halogens are missing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining useful aromatic and polar arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need bond-environment awareness and conventional alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from local scores. Distinguish ordinary aryl fluorination from heteroatom-halogen substitution, and free nitrogen centres from acylated or sulfonyl-bound ones. This chemistry comparison does not establish that a universal filter improves scores or that a particular component caused the liabilities.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The geometric-feasibility gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was reproduced in n-62daf219c70a under the supplied Search panel. Current n-c2f46c40bbba adds a dense nitrogen cage with small-ring connections, a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring, and crowded bridged dicarbonyl systems. Its leading cage is noncumulated, so the historical small cyclic-cumulene example is source-specific and is not asserted to describe this Child leader. Conventional linked aza-aromatics and indole amides remain counterexamples to a universal ring-geometry failure.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot reliably turn valid ring connectivity into geometrically credible, accessible ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need to account for ring size, unsaturation and bridge connectivity while offering feasible alternatives that retain learned functional arrangements. Aromatic labels and ring counts alone cannot supply this information. Preserve legitimate fused and small-ring chemistry; no blanket ring prohibition or established score gain follows from these observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, and remains present in n-c2f46c40bbba on the same supplied Search Seeds and observation budget. Every current digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, while saturated nitrogen rings, substituted methines and cage junctions visibly admit unresolved stereochemical possibilities. Formal-charge incidence is also 0.0, but free amines do occur; that is a separate state-representation issue.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated or bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations should preserve or resolve stereochemical identity when the structure requires it, while distinguishing achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, tautomerism and alkene geometry separately. The present observations establish unspecified identity rather than a measured stereochemical score penalty or a component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was retained in n-62daf219c70a. Under the current matched Search conditions, n-c2f46c40bbba proposes more molecules with at most four heavy atoms in every supplied stream than the Parent. Methane, interhalogens, peroxide chains and small heteroatom fragments recur late. At the other extreme an 86-heavy-atom repeated heteroaromatic assembly scores 0.6003060183611016 while a 32-heavy-atom linked heterocycle scores 0.6043543077209765 in the same seed. Compact useful structures are already possible; the problem is inconsistent context retention and simplification.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful molecular context while avoiding fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to preserve favorable combinations of functional regions while testing simplification or replacement of dispensable parts. A task-agnostic generator needs controlled fragment loss and context-preserving alternatives rather than a universal minimum size or an automatic preference for larger molecules. These conditional associations do not identify the responsible search component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This coverage gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; n-c2f46c40bbba provides current evidence under the matched Search panel. Leaders recur as indole/anilide, linked aza-aromatic, aryl/sulfur, dicarbonyl-polycycle or nitrogen-cage relatives. Different seeds do reach different families, including open diaryl frameworks and small nonaromatic oxygen rings, so there is no global scaffold collapse or inability to form new rings. High unique-SMILES counts also include unusual bonds, fragments and elaborations, which are not equivalent to useful feasible alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce chemically independent, plausible alternatives to a leading family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic scaffold transformations should reorganize learned functional-group relationships into independently connected, chemically plausible alternatives and assess them through ordinary local feedback. Structural association is not proof that more diversity improves the objective, that the generator lacks any specific group, or that the current component intervention caused family concentration.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
